key_insight: PWLNet makes neural process surrogates optimization-compatible through exact or piecewise-linear reformulations, with compact models enabling tractable optimization.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can embed learned steady-state and dynamic process models in Pyomo to optimize operating conditions and control policies.
method: Train baseline or physics-informed networks and prune hidden neurons for optimization efficiency.
Embed ReLU, exact-tanh, or PWL-tanh models using MILP, nonlinear, or binary-free SOSX formulations.
Use PWL-native training to match training and embedding activations, avoiding added linearization error.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks, reported results include 6.5× faster Williams–Otto MILP solves after 15% pruning and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy for Van de Vusse.
watch_item: Constraint fidelity remains a concern: hydroformylation exact-tanh control reached 20.002 bar against a 20-bar limit, and longer horizons or physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results.
paper_title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
